title: Stool test (coprogram)
what: A small amount of stool is looked at under a microscope. It shows how food is digested and whether there is inflammation.
why: For belly pain, bloating, diarrhea or constipation, or if digestive problems are suspected.
duration: collecting at home takes a few minutes; results usually take 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially laxatives, iron, digestive enzymes, and antibiotics
If you recently had a barium X-ray or a colonoscopy

prepare.title: Container
prepare.text: Buy a sterile container with a small spoon at a pharmacy, or get one from the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Laxatives, suppositories, and enemas are usually not used for 2 to 3 days before the test. If you need them, tell your doctor and they will decide.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually eat as normal. Sometimes the doctor gives you a special diet for a few days. Follow it.

prepare.title: For women
prepare.text: It is better to put off the test during your period.

steps: First pass urine, so it does not mix with the stool
Have a bowel movement into a clean, dry bedpan or onto clean plastic wrap, not from the toilet
With the spoon in the lid, take bits from different spots, about the size of a walnut
Close the container tightly and label it
Take it to the lab the same day
after: If you cannot take it right away, the container is usually kept in the fridge, not the freezer, for a few hours. Check how long with the lab
Your doctor will explain the result
red_flags: Black, tar-like stool or a lot of blood in your stool: see a doctor right away or call emergency services
Severe belly pain with fever or vomiting: see a doctor the same day

faq.q: Can I collect the stool the evening before?
faq.a: A morning sample is better. If you only have an evening one, keep it in the fridge and bring it in the morning. Check the time limit with the lab.
Not much. About a third of the container, the size of a walnut.

reminders.text: Stool test tomorrow. Get a sterile container and a clean, dry bedpan ready.
